adapter.description: `legacy`, the default, is deprecated since v1.74.0 and still ships: migrate with `sluis migrate`. checksum.description: The integrity header of every upload: `sha256` (x-amz-checksum-sha256, computed over the whole body and sent precomputed, never as an aws-chunked trailer), `md5` (Content-MD5) or `none`, for a store that refuses SHA-256. credentials.description: Instead of a static document, sluis mints its own R2 credentials from a Cloudflare preset: the account's minter credential clones the preset's prototype, the credentials are renewed with a third of their lifetime left and minted again once after a 403. Exclusive with `credentialsRef`. Needs `endpoint`, the ssm secrets source, and the `cloudflare` section.

preset.description: A key of `cloudflare.presets` that has an `endpoint` (an R2 preset).

credentialsRef.description: Where the credentials for `endpoint` are, in the installation's secrets store (the ssm secrets source): the internal address, `internal/<module>/<name>`, of the `s3-credentials/v1` document (`access_key_id`, `secret_access_key`) that holds static credentials, or `external/cloudflare/<preset>`, the `cloudflare/v1` document the Cloudflare module rotates for an R2 preset with `store: external` (the access key is the token's id; it is read again with a third of its time left and after a 403). endpoint.description: Overrides the S3 address: LocalStack or an S3-compatible store (Cloudflare R2, MinIO).

pathStyle.description: Addresses the bucket in the path and not the host name, which LocalStack and most S3-compatible stores need.

prefix.description: A key prefix inside the bucket, for an installation that shares it.

region.description: The bucket's region. Absent, the SDK's own resolution (`AWS_REGION`).

dynamodb.description: The DynamoDB tables of the `dynamodb` adapter: one table per module (`tables`, layout v5). create.description: Create the table (on-demand, TTL on `expires`) at start when it is not there, for a test or a development installation. layout.description: `ssm`, required: the storage layout of the installation's secrets, `v5`, the only one: the module first, `<root>/internal/<module>/` and `<root>/external/<module>/` (docs/decisions/0072-storage-layout-v5-module-first.md). readCache.description: `ssm`: how long a process keeps a document it read; a write drops it. `0s` is off. SLUIS_SECRETS_READ_CACHE_TTL overrides.

refresh.description: `ssm`: how old a secret's copy may be before it is read again: a rotated secret reaches every instance within it.

region.description: `ssm`: the region. Unset follows the AWS SDK's own resolution.

root.description: `file`: the directory the secrets are mounted under. `ssm`: the installation's root, /sluis/<instance>.

source.description: `env`: the variable SLUIS_SECRET_<NAME> (the name upper-cased, every other character an underscore), for a local run. `file`: the file <root>/<name>, read on every use, so a rotated mount takes effect without a restart. `ssm`: a SecureString in AWS SSM Parameter Store under <root> (/sluis/<instance>), on layout v5 (`layout`): a name the service knows is read at its module's address (`<root>/internal/oidc/state-secret`, ...), any other at `<root>/internal/config/<name>`.

grace.description: `ssm`: how long the previous value of a rotated client secret is still accepted: the document's previous revision, while the current one is younger than this (docs/decisions/0039-the-issuer-generates-confidential-client-secrets.md, the overlap).

kmsKeyId.description: `ssm`: the id, ARN or alias of the customer-managed KMS key the parameters the service itself writes (its credentials) are encrypted with. Unset, the AWS-managed `alias/aws/ssm`. The `ssm` secrets adapter's `kmsKeyId` setting; naming another there is refused.

layout.description: `ssm`, required: the storage layout of the installation's secrets, `v5`, the only one: the module first, `<root>/internal/<module>/` and `<root>/external/<module>/` (docs/decisions/0072-storage-layout-v5-module-first.md). Layout `v4` was removed in v1.77.1 (an installation still on it migrates with `sluis migrate v5` of v1.77.0 first), and with it the reading of an absent layout as `v4`.

readCache.description: `ssm`: how long a process keeps a document it read; a write drops it. `0s` is off. SLUIS_SECRETS_READ_CACHE_TTL overrides.

refresh.description: `ssm`: how old a secret's copy may be before it is read again: a rotated secret reaches every instance within it.

region.description: `ssm`: the region. Unset follows the AWS SDK's own resolution.

root.description: `file`: the directory the secrets are mounted under. `ssm`: the installation's root, /sluis/<instance>.

source.description: `env`: the variable SLUIS_SECRET_<NAME> (the name upper-cased, every other character an underscore), for a local run. `file`: the file <root>/<name>, read on every use, so a rotated mount takes effect without a restart. `ssm`: a SecureString in AWS SSM Parameter Store under <root> (/sluis/<instance>), on layout v5 (`layout`): a name the service knows is read at its module's address (`<root>/internal/oidc/state-secret`, ...), any other at `<root>/internal/config/<name>`.

slack.description: The Slack module's routing (docs/decisions/0071). Unset keeps the module in this process.

remote.description: Where the Slack module is when it is not this process: the calls to it go there. Set exactly one of `function` and `url`. Unset keeps the module in this process.

audience.description: The audience of that token. The module's name, `slack`, when unset.

function.description: The module's Lambda function, name or ARN. It is invoked through the `live-<class>` alias of this process's caller class.

tokenFile.description: Where the projected token is mounted. `/var/run/secrets/sluis/slack/token` when unset.

url.description: The module's Kubernetes Service. A call carries the pod's projected ServiceAccount token.

serve.description: Makes the Slack module answer the issuer's calls on Kubernetes (docs/decisions/0071). Only the module's own document sets it. The module listens on `address` and accepts a call whose projected ServiceAccount token was minted for `audience`, checked with a TokenReview, and whose subject is one of `issuers`; any other call is a 401. On Lambda the function answers `rpc` events and IAM decides who may invoke it. Not with `remote`. Unset serves nothing.

address.description: The listener, `host:port`; it also answers `GET /healthz`. `:8081` when unset.

audience.description: The audience a caller's token must be minted for. The module's name, `slack`, when unset.

issuers.description: The issuer's ServiceAccount, as `system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:<name>`. A call from it is both the issuer class (`mint_installation`) and the console class (the console methods); a token of any other subject is a 401.

tokenFile.description: This pod's projected ServiceAccount token, presented to the console and read afresh on every call.

config-policy.description: The policy document: what an installation decides, read by every process of it. The access model's tables (docs/reference/sluis/policy.md) and beside them whom the exchange trusts, what an operator may make, what each controller may change and what is copied out. Rendered by `sluisctl policy render` from layers; a process reads exactly one. Nothing here is a secret.

apps.description: What an operator may make on the console.

Every GitHub App the installation declares, of every purpose: the link App, the catalogue Apps and the runner tiers (docs/guides/sluis/connect/github-apps-catalogue.md). A grant naming an undeclared group stops the service.

items.description: One App. A `catalogue` entry needs `org` and `permissions`; a `runner` entry needs `tier` and declares nothing of a catalogue App's; the `link` entry has the id `link`.

events.description: Webhook events the App subscribes to. They are delivered only to an App that declares a `webhook`.

export.description: Place the installed App's key at `external/github/<id>` for a consumer to read. Unset keeps it internal. A runner App is always exported.

grants.description: Who may ask for tokens of it, and for how much.

permissions.description: Permission name to level: read, write or admin.

id.description: The App's key in storage, unique, never changes. `link` for the link App; for a catalogue App [a-z0-9-], at most 32, not beginning `runner-`; a runner entry may leave it out (`runner-<tier>`, and `runner-<tier>-<org>` with an `org`).

labels.description: At most 16 short lower-case labels, key to value, kept on the App's record for a reader that selects Apps by them.

name.description: The App's name on GitHub, at most 34. A catalogue App's default is <org>-<id>; the `link` App's and an organisation's have a built-in default, cut to the limit. A runner entry takes none.

org.description: The organisation a catalogue App is created under (required for it), or the only organisation of a runner entry (no `org` offers the tier in every organisation). The link App's owner.

permissions.description: Permission name to level: read, write or admin.

purpose.description: What the App is for: `link` is the App that links a person's GitHub account, `catalogue` an App an operator creates and installs from the console, `runner` the tier an operator may create a runner App for.

tier.description: A runner entry's tier: lower-case letters, digits and dashes, at most 16.

webhook.description: Where GitHub delivers the App's events: exactly one of `url` and `kargo`. Needs non-empty `events`; set `export: true` so a consumer can read the secret. The secret is generated by this service, set on GitHub right after the App is created, and kept at `external/github/<id>` as `webhook_secret`; it is rotated from the console, without overlap (docs/decisions/0041). An App created before this is declared cannot be switched to a webhook: GitHub has no API for that, so disconnect it and create it again.

project.description: The Kargo project; empty for a cluster-scoped receiver.

receiver.description: The receiver's name in the Kargo project.

url.description: The endpoint every delivery is POSTed to, e.g. Argo CD's `https://argocd.example/api/webhook`.

workspace.description: A key of the policy's slack.workspaces.

backup.description: Who may start a backup through the issuer, from the console or `sluisctl backup run`. Reading the status, the list and a restore needs the viewer role and is not named here. A restore is never started through the issuer.

runGroups.description: Groups of this policy: every holder may start a backup. Empty or unset lets nobody; the operators group is not implied.

additionalProperties.description: A claims fragment: merged into the token (docs/reference/sluis/policy.md#claims).

claims.description: What a group adds to a token, by group.

client_documents.description: Admits clients that are not declared, by a document they serve about themselves. Off unless it names an origin.

groups.description: Which held groups beyond the requires pairs a token for it carries: `all`, or a list of things, families or names (docs/reference/sluis/policy.md#groups-in-a-token-scoping).

requires.description: The groups a caller must hold.

session.description: Every document client's refresh chains: `interactive` (a person at a browser, the installation's `lifetimes`) or `agent` (software that holds its refresh token and works in the background, the service's `lifetimes.agent`). Recorded on each chain when its authorization completes (docs/decisions/0040). Never read from a document: admit with `agent` only an origin whose documents its vendor controls.

additionalProperties.description: A client: who may be issued a token, and for what. Its id is the audience.

backchannel_logout_uri.description: Where a back-channel logout is posted.

description.description: One line about it on the sign-in page. Public.

display_name.description: What the sign-in page calls it. Public.

groups.description: Which held groups beyond the requires pairs a token for it carries: `all`, or a list of things, families or names (docs/reference/sluis/policy.md#groups-in-a-token-scoping).

harness.description: A conformance or test harness signs in through it: the only kind of client the conformance account (`conformance.enabled`) may sign in to. Refused on an exchange client.

pkce.description: Whether it must use PKCE (RFC 7636, RFC 9700 2.1.1): `required` refuses an authorization request with no S256 `code_challenge` and a code redeemed with no `code_verifier`. A public client is always `required` and refuses `optional`; absent is `optional` for a confidential client. Refused on an exchange client.

redirects.description: The redirect URIs. Plain `http://` only to `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]` or `localhost`.

requires.description: The groups a caller must hold, any of them.

secret.description: For a confidential client: the name its secret is delivered under, or `{generate: true}` to have the issuer generate it and keep it with its credentials.

generate.description: Must be true; `generate: false` is refused.

secretKey.description: The chart's: the key of the Secret `secret` names that holds the client's secret. Default client-secret. Not rendered into the policy document.

session.description: Its refresh chains: `interactive` (a person at a browser, the installation's `lifetimes`) or `agent` (software that holds its refresh token and works in the background, the service's `lifetimes.agent`). Recorded on each chain when its authorization completes (docs/decisions/0040). Refused on an exchange client and, as `agent`, with `sign_in_exchange`.

sign_in_exchange.description: It may exchange a sign-in for a token of its own.

signed_out.description: Where sign-out may return the browser. Plain `http://` as for `redirects`.

signing_alg.description: The algorithm its tokens are signed with, when it cannot verify the default: RS256, ES256 or ES384.

ttl_cap.description: The longest a token for it lives.

clients.description: Who may be issued a token, by client id.

cloudflare.description: Who may ask for a Cloudflare preset (the presets are the service document's `cloudflare.presets`). A preset named here and not there stops the service.

group.description: A group of this policy: every holder may ask, a person from the console or `sluisctl`, a CI job through the exchange. A CI job is a group declared with `github` matchers.

controllers.description: What each controller may CHANGE. Everything else the policy binds is derived every pass and shown with what would happen, and left alone: an organisation or workspace is born disabled.

appNames.description: For an organisation the github table binds, the name its App is created with on GitHub (at most 34 characters). Optional: an organisation with no entry gets the built-in default, cut to the limit. An App already created keeps the name it has.

appRefs.description: For an organisation the github table binds, the id of the catalogue App (in `apps.github.apps`, created under that organisation) whose key its record refers to, `app_ref`. Optional: an organisation whose record already names an App keeps it, so an entry only overrides it or declares an organisation anew.

enabledOrgs.description: The organisations it changes. Each must be bound by the github table.

enabledWorkspaces.description: The workspaces it changes, by key. Each must be declared by the outline table. The rest are dry runs.
The workspaces it changes, by key. Each must be declared by the slack table.

exchange.description: Whom the token exchange trusts. Nothing here is a secret: every row is a name and a URL.

aws.description: The AWS accounts whose roles' outbound identity tokens (sts:GetWebIdentityToken) are verified. An empty list verifies none.

name.description: The estate's word for it, for logs.

audience.description: The audience the role must request. Required with an account: it is the trust boundary.

clusters.description: The clusters whose ServiceAccount tokens are verified, each against the key set it publishes for itself. This service's own cluster is a row like any other.

jwksUri.description: Where its keys are. Unset discovers them from the issuer.

owners.description: The organisations. None verifies none: an empty list would admit every repository there is.

repositoryIds.description: The numeric ids of the repositories whose tokens are verified (the token's `repository_id`). When set, a token must carry one of them. Unset asks nothing of the id.

match.description: The identity the limit is about: one matcher, as a group's, matched against the proof alone. Exactly one kind is set.

config-sluis.description: The configuration of `sluis serve`, the one process of sluis: the issuer, the console and the directory hub and, under `controllers`, the GitHub and Slack controllers. On Kubernetes it is one Deployment; on AWS Lambda it is one function. Secrets are never in this file: a field ending in ...Secret holds the NAME of a secret, which `secrets` says how to deliver, and a field ending in ...File holds a path (a credential the platform mounts and rotates). Telemetry is the OTEL_* environment, not configuration.

allowInsecure.description: Accept a plain-http issuer URL, for a local run. When the issuer URL is also on the loopback interface (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`), the issuer connects to loopback and private addresses when it fetches client documents and posts back-channel logouts; with any other issuer URL those guards stay on.

audit.description: The audit installation this service records to. Unset keeps the trail in the log only.

audience.description: The client whose audience the Audit page's tokens carry.

forwardedForTrustedHops.description: How many of the deployment's own proxies append to X-Forwarded-For; zero records the peer.

queryURL.description: The query service, for the console's Audit page. Its own setting: it needs no `writer`, so the page works with the `sqs` and `log` sinks. A path prefix (`https://audit.example/sluis`) is kept and the procedure path appended.

tokenFile.description: This workload's projected service-account token, presented on every call.

cloudflare.description: sluis as the STS for Cloudflare API tokens and R2 credentials (docs/guides/sluis/cloudflare-tokens.md). Cloudflare has no web-identity federation, so sluis holds one minter credential per account and hands out short-lived account tokens cloned from a DISABLED prototype token. Needs the ssm secrets source. Unset is off.

minter.description: The internal address of the minter credential, `internal/cloudflare/<account>/minter`: a cloudflare-minter/v1 document holding an account token that has Account API Tokens Read and Edit and nothing else. It is never an external address: nobody but sluis is granted it.

accounts.description: The Cloudflare accounts sluis mints in, by the name presets use.

forbiddenPermissionGroups.description: Permission groups, by the name Cloudflare lists them under, that a prototype may never grant, IN ADDITION to the built-in list: Account API Tokens Edit (Write), Billing, Account Settings, Memberships, and Access: Organizations, Identity Providers, and Groups. The built-in list is the only thing between the minter and everything its creator could do, so it cannot be shortened by configuration, only extended.

additionalProperties.description: One preset: a prototype token and how long its clones live.

allowedPermissionGroups.description: Limits the prototype to these permission groups, by the name Cloudflare lists them under (case and spacing do not matter). A prototype that grants any other is refused with `prototype_forbidden`. Unset asks nothing beyond the built-in list. The built-in list and `forbiddenPermissionGroups` stay the floor: a name here does not lift them. Prefer setting it: the built-in list names five kinds of group, and Cloudflare adds new ones.

description.description: What the preset is for. Shown by the console and `sluisctl whoami`.

endpoint.description: Makes this an R2 preset: the S3 endpoint of the account (`https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`, or `https://<account-id>.eu.r2.cloudflarestorage.com` for an EU jurisdiction). The stored document then holds an access key and secret instead of a token.

lifetime.description: How long each minted token lives: its `expires_on`. At least 1m, at most 24h. Past it sluis deletes the token in Cloudflare.

maxLive.description: How many unexpired on-demand tokens this preset may have in all, whoever holds them; a mint over it is refused (`preset_cap`). Cloudflare allows an account 500 tokens in all, and an expired one counts until it is deleted. The record of minted tokens holds about 65 on-demand tokens, so a value above about 60 is refused as `record_full` first. Unset is 50.

maxLivePerCaller.description: How many unexpired on-demand tokens of this preset one caller may hold; a mint over it is refused (`caller_cap`). Unset is 10.

maxMintsPerCallerPerHour.description: How many tokens of this preset one caller may be minted in an hour; one over it is refused (`rate_limited`). Counted from the preset's record of minted tokens and from this process's own mints, so a token that expired inside the hour and was deleted is only counted where it was minted. Unset is 30.

prototype.description: The id of the prototype: an account token in Cloudflare that is DISABLED and whose policies and condition are the preset's rights. An active prototype is refused (it would be a usable token that never expires), and so is one granting Account API Tokens Edit, Billing, Account Settings, Memberships or Access identity providers. It is read at every mint, so editing it applies at the next rotation.

rotation.description: How often the stored token is replaced. At least 1m and shorter than `lifetime`: `lifetime - rotation` is the time consumers have to pick up a new token. Required unless `store` is `none`, and then left out.

store.description: Where the schedule keeps this preset's token. `external` rotates it into `external/cloudflare/<preset>` for consumers to read. `none` keeps nothing: the schedule never mints it, no parameter exists for it, and a token is minted only on demand (`sluisctl cloudflare token <preset>`) for a caller the policy's grants allow.

presets.description: What may be minted, by name (a DNS label). The name is in the external address, `external/cloudflare/<preset>`, and in the name of every token minted for it.

remote.description: Where the minter is when it is not this process: the on-demand token exchange calls the Cloudflare module there (docs/decisions/0071), and this document then declares no `accounts` or `presets`. Set exactly one of `function` and `url`. Unset keeps the minter in this process.

audience.description: The audience of that token. The module's name, `cloudflare`, when unset.

function.description: The module's Lambda function, name or ARN. It is invoked through its `live-issuer` alias.

tokenFile.description: Where the projected token is mounted. `/var/run/secrets/sluis/cloudflare/token` when unset.

url.description: The module's Kubernetes Service. A call carries the pod's projected ServiceAccount token.

serve.description: Makes the Cloudflare module answer other modules' calls (docs/decisions/0071): the issuer's token exchange when its `remote` names this module. On Kubernetes the module listens on `address` and accepts a call that carries a projected ServiceAccount token minted for `audience`, checked with a TokenReview; any other call is a 401. On Lambda the function answers `rpc` events, and IAM decides who may invoke it. Needs `presets`; not with `remote`. Unset serves nothing.

address.description: The listener on Kubernetes, `host:port`; it also answers `GET /healthz`. Unused on Lambda.

audience.description: The audience a caller's token must be minted for. The module's name, `cloudflare`, when unset.

issuers.description: The issuer's ServiceAccount, as `system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:<name>`, which may call the listener on Kubernetes. A call from it is both the issuer class (the mint) and the console class; a token of any other subject is a 401. The listener refuses to start with none. Unused on Lambda.

tick.description: How often the rotation looks at the presets: the interval of the schedule that invokes it on Lambda (the library fills it from `CloudflareRotation` when unset), a minute for the Kubernetes loop. A credential rotates up to one tick after its preset's `rotation`, so the console calls one overdue only past `rotation + tick`; make `rotation` a multiple of the tick to rotate when intended. Unset is a minute.

cluster.description: Names this cluster in a ServiceAccount's subject. A pod cannot discover it; unset keeps the older unqualified subject.

conformance.description: The test account of the OpenID conformance harness: a non-privileged subject that signs in with a username and password, only to clients the policy marks `harness`, and only while enabled. Off unless turned on (docs/decisions/0076).

enabled.description: Turn the account on. The sign-in page offers it only for a request of a client marked `harness`; a Lambda stack also generates its password and verifier.

verifierSecret.description: The secret the account's SRP verifier is (`conformance/verifier`): a salt and a verifier, never the password.

console.description: Where the console is published, for the sign-in that starts there.

awsAudience.description: The audience an AWS role's web identity token must be minted for to be a bearer at the console (a Lambda controller). Its own, distinct from the AWS federation file's, so a token for token exchange is no proof here and the reverse. Default `<issuerURL>/console`.

backup.description: Connects the console's Backups page to the backup module and the restore function (docs/decisions/0071). The console only reads from them, as the caller class `console`. Unset has no page.

audience.description: The audience of the projected token. Each module's name when unset.

function.description: The backup module's Lambda function, name or ARN, invoked through its `live-console` alias. Set exactly one of `function` and `url`.

restoreFunction.description: The restore function, name or ARN, invoked through its `live-console` alias. At most one of it and `restoreURL`; without either the page says there is none.

tokenFile.description: Where the projected token is mounted. `/var/run/secrets/sluis/backup/token` when unset.

url.description: The backup module's Kubernetes Service. A call carries the pod's projected ServiceAccount token.

client.description: The client id the console signs in as.

origin.description: The console's origin, when it is not the issuer's.

controllers.description: The controllers this process runs beside the issuer and the console, each in its own loop. A controller that is absent is off. Which organisations and workspaces a running controller may CHANGE is the policy document's `controllers.<kind>.enabledOrgs` and `enabledWorkspaces`, as before. A controller reads the console's API as a workload, so the policy's exchange must admit its proof (a ServiceAccount token on Kubernetes, the function role's web identity token on Lambda).

github.description: The GitHub controller: makes each GitHub organisation's teams match the policy's github table.

appsDir.description: One file per connected organisation: its App's credentials. Read only with `ports.adapter: legacy`; with another adapter they are on the State port.

console.description: How the controller proves itself to the console, when the pod's `tokenFile` is not the way.

recordsDir.description: The console's records, mounted. Read only with `ports.adapter: legacy`.

freshness.description: How the directory's snapshot is kept current.

groupsScoping.description: How far this installation has moved toward per-audience `groups` scoping: `off`, `report` or `enforce`.

hsts.description: The Strict-Transport-Security header the issuer and the console send on a response that arrived over https. Never `preload`; never sent over http or to a loopback host.

includeSubDomains.description: Extend the rule to the host's subdomains. Off by default: an issuer on an apex or parent domain would pin every sibling subdomain to https for `maxAge`. Turn it on only when every subdomain answers https.

maxAge.description: How long a browser keeps the rule, in whole seconds. Zero sends no header.

inCluster.description: Prove recovery against the cluster the pod runs in. Set by a deployment that turns recovery on.

issuerURL.description: The issuer: baked into every token and every relying party's trust, so there is no default. No trailing slash is kept.

archive.description: Deprecated, ignored: the archive key of backup format 1. Accepted so a document that still sets it loads; backups are age-encrypted to `backup.recipients`.

keys.title: keys

lifetimes.description: How long what the issuer hands out lives.

absolute.description: A session, at most. Positive, and at least `token`: a session has to end SOMETIME after sign-in, and an access token cannot outlive the session that grants it.

agent.description: The refresh chains of clients the policy marks `session: agent`, such as MCP hosts (docs/decisions/0040). Their chains are held to these instead of `refresh` and `absolute`.

absolute.description: An agent chain, at most, from `auth_time`. Positive, and at most 2160h (90 days).

access.description: The longest an agent client's access or ID token lives. Positive, and at most 1h.

refresh.description: An agent chain's idle limit. Positive, and at most `absolute`.

hold.description: How long a removal is held before it takes effect.

session.description: The console's own session cookie, capped at `absolute`.

listen.description: A TCP listener. `address` is a host:port the service binds; an empty host binds every interface.

log.description: Structured logging. One level for the whole service: per-package levels are deliberately not part of the contract.

level.description: The lowest level that is written.

login.description: How a person signs in to the console.

directory.description: Sign in with the corporate directory.

forwarded.description: A sign-in an authenticating proxy has already done.

audience.description: The audience its token carries.

emailHeader.description: The header that carries the signed-in address.

oauthClient.description: The OAuth client registered once with the directory backend: it drives both admin consent and operator sign-in.

id.description: The client id, for a local run. Not a secret.

idKey.description: The key of the id in that Secret.

provider.description: Names the client's secrets: providers/google/<provider>/client-secret, and providers/google/<provider>/client-id unless `id` gives it. One segment of a secret's name.

secretKey.description: The key of the secret in that Secret.

secretName.description: The Kubernetes Secret the client is declared in, which the console shows and cannot change.

outline.description: The Outline module's routing (docs/decisions/0077). The issuer never runs the module: unset, the console's Outline pages say there is none.

remote.description: Where the Outline module is: the console's Outline pages are its. Set exactly one of `function` and `url`.

audience.description: The audience of that token. The module's name, `outline`, when unset.

function.description: The module's Lambda function, name or ARN. It is invoked through the `live-<class>` alias of this process's caller class.

tokenFile.description: Where the projected token is mounted. `/var/run/secrets/sluis/outline/token` when unset.

url.description: The module's Kubernetes Service. A call carries the pod's projected ServiceAccount token.

platform.description: What this installation has to build on. The answers pick a preset (the decision tree in docs/concepts/sluis/ports.md), and start refuses an adapter that needs an answer that is no. Absent, the `ports` keys decide and nothing is checked against the platform.

aws.description: AWS is available: its credentials, DynamoDB, S3, SSM, KMS, SQS and EventBridge.

replicas.description: How many replicas share this installation's state. Above 1 start refuses an adapter that keeps its data in the process (`memory`).

runtime.description: Where sluis itself runs. Absent: `kubernetes` with a cluster, else `lambda` on AWS, else `process`.

policy.description: The policy document this service decides by. Unset is the built-in two groups, or the demonstration policy under `demo`.

file.description: The policy document: the one canonical file `sluisctl policy render` writes (schemas/config/policy.schema.json). Read once, at start: a change is a new instance.

ports.description: The adapters behind the storage ports (docs/concepts/sluis/ports.md).

adapter.description: `legacy`, the default, is deprecated since v1.74.0 and still ships: migrate with `sluis migrate`. It keeps state where it has always been kept: the namespace's ConfigMaps and Secrets and, when `valkey` is set, Valkey. `memory` keeps all of it in this process, which a restart loses: for a local run and the demonstration, and not with `store: kubernetes` or `valkey`.  `dynamodb` keeps the same in one DynamoDB table (`ports.dynamodb`), with the platform's credentials, and takes its Blob from `legacy` unless `ports.blob` names its own.

blob.description: Replaces the Blob port (status reports, directory snapshots) with an adapter of its own, whatever `ports.adapter` is. Absent, the Blob is `ports.adapter`'s.

adapter.description: `s3` keeps the blobs in an S3 bucket.

s3.description: Where the S3 adapter keeps its objects. Credentials are the platform's (EKS Pod Identity, IRSA, a Lambda role) and are never configured here.

bucket.description: The bucket. It must exist, with public access blocked.

checksum.description: The integrity header of every upload: `sha256` (x-amz-checksum-sha256, computed over the whole body and sent precomputed, never as an aws-chunked trailer), `md5` (Content-MD5) or `none`, for a store that refuses SHA-256. AWS refuses a PutObject without one on an Object Lock bucket.

credentials.description: Instead of a static document, sluis mints its own R2 credentials from a Cloudflare preset: the account's minter credential clones the preset's prototype, the credentials are renewed with a third of their lifetime left and minted again once after a 403. Exclusive with `credentialsRef`. Needs `endpoint`, the ssm secrets source, and the `cloudflare` section.

preset.description: A key of `cloudflare.presets` that has an `endpoint` (an R2 preset).

credentialsRef.description: Where the credentials for `endpoint` are, in the installation's secrets store (the ssm secrets source): the internal address, `internal/<module>/<name>`, of the `s3-credentials/v1` document (`access_key_id`, `secret_access_key`) that holds static credentials, or `external/cloudflare/<preset>`, the `cloudflare/v1` document the Cloudflare module rotates for an R2 preset with `store: external` (the access key is the token's id; it is read again with a third of its time left and after a 403). Read at start and again after an answer of 403, at most once a minute. Needs `endpoint`; `region` defaults to `auto` with it. Any other address is refused. This is the simple way and needs no `cloudflare` section in this document, so it is the one to use when the presets are another module's (`cloudflare.remote`).

endpoint.description: Overrides the S3 address: LocalStack or an S3-compatible store (Cloudflare R2, MinIO).

kmsKey.description: A KMS key id, ARN or alias for server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) of every write. Absent, the bucket's default encryption applies.

pathStyle.description: Addresses the bucket in the path and not the host name, which LocalStack and most S3-compatible stores need.

prefix.description: A key prefix inside the bucket, for an installation that shares it.

region.description: The bucket's region. Absent, the SDK's own resolution (`AWS_REGION`).

dynamodb.description: The DynamoDB tables of the `dynamodb` adapter: one table per module (`tables`, layout v5). Each has a string partition key `pk`, a string sort key `sk` and the TTL attribute `expires`. Credentials are the platform's (EKS Pod Identity, IRSA, a Lambda role) and are never configured here; an S3-compatible `endpoint` with no such identity names a credentials document by address (`credentialsRef`), never by value.

create.description: Create the table (on-demand, TTL on `expires`) at start when it is not there, for a test or a development installation. Off, the table must exist: production uses the one the infrastructure code made, and the role needs `dynamodb:DescribeTable` on it (layout v5: the readiness probe asks, not the start).

endpoint.description: Overrides the DynamoDB address: LocalStack or DynamoDB Local.

region.description: The table's region. Absent, the SDK's own resolution (`AWS_REGION`).

tables.description: Layout v5 (docs/decisions/0072-storage-layout-v5-module-first.md): the table of each module, by module name. A process names its own module's table and the tables of the peers it reads; a module it does not name is not opened. The single table of layout v4 (`table`) was removed in v1.77.1.

backup.description: The name of the backup module's table. The library default is `sluis-<instance>-backup`.

cloudflare.description: The name of the cloudflare module's table. The library default is `sluis-<instance>-cloudflare`.

github.description: The name of the github module's table. The library default is `sluis-<instance>-github`.

google.description: The name of the google module's table. The library default is `sluis-<instance>-google`.

oidc.description: The name of the oidc module's table. The library default is `sluis-<instance>-oidc`.

outline.description: The name of the outline module's table. The library default is `sluis-<instance>-outline`.

slack.description: The name of the slack module's table. The library default is `sluis-<instance>-slack`.

preset.description: The adapters of a whole platform, one per concern: `server` (no AWS, no Kubernetes), `k8s-minimal`, `k8s-openbao`, `aws-serverless`, `aws-hybrid` (sluis on Lambda, a cluster for the workloads), `k8s-aws` (sluis as a pod on Kubernetes with AWS storage: DynamoDB, S3, KMS-wrapped signing; SSM secrets, or OpenBao with `adapters.secrets`). `aws-eks` is the deprecated name of `k8s-aws`. Absent, the preset the `platform` answers lead to; with neither, the `ports` keys decide. `adapters` and the `ports` keys override single concerns.

probes.description: The health listener. Separate from the service's own traffic, so that readiness is answerable when the service's listener is saturated, and so that a probe is not reachable from outside.

publicRootURL.description: The host's root, never carrying the console's mount: the bootstrap surface stays there. Unset follows `publicURL`.

publicURL.description: Where a browser reaches the console, including its mount. The admin-consent redirect URI and the values the setup steps show are built from it. Default http://localhost:8081.

recovery.description: The sign-in that needs no directory: in a cluster, a token for a ServiceAccount proven against the API server; anywhere else, a password. Unset is off for the issuer and, for the hub, on.

audience.description: The audience its token must carry.

enabled.description: Turn recovery on. Needs `inCluster`, `serviceAccount` and `audience` to be usable.

generation.description: Names this configuration's decision to have recovery on. An operator may disable recovery from the console (only after signing in through the identity provider); the disable is kept in the State against the generation in force and covers only it. A redeploy of the same document keeps recovery disabled; change this value, to any other string, to turn it back on. Unset is the generation `""`.

passwordSecret.description: Outside a cluster: the secret the recovery password is (`recovery/password`), read to derive the account's SRP verifier, which is all the hub holds of it, unless `verifierSecret` names one (docs/decisions/0076). Unset generates one and prints it, except on a function, where recovery is then off. `enabled: false` leaves it untouched and refuses the sign-in, so turning it back on needs no new password.

serviceAccount.description: The ServiceAccount whose token signs in.

verifierSecret.description: Outside a cluster: the secret the recovery account's SRP verifier is (`recovery/verifier`): a salt and a verifier, never the password. The sign-in page proves knowledge of the password against it without sending it (docs/decisions/0076). Unset derives one from the password at start.

release.description: The name this installation's objects carry: the Kubernetes object names (`<release>-github-orgs`, ...) and the prefix of its keys in a shared store. The chart requires it to be the release's full name.

secrets.description: How the secrets this document names are delivered (truvity/policy config.md section 5). Absent is `env`.

endpoint.description: `ssm`: overrides the SSM address, for LocalStack.

grace.description: `ssm`: how long the previous value of a rotated client secret is still accepted: the document's previous revision, while the current one is younger than this (docs/decisions/0039-the-issuer-generates-confidential-client-secrets.md, the overlap).

kmsKeyId.description: `ssm`: the id, ARN or alias of the customer-managed KMS key the parameters the service itself writes (its credentials) are encrypted with. Unset, the AWS-managed `alias/aws/ssm`. The `ssm` secrets adapter's `kmsKeyId` setting; naming another there is refused.

layout.description: `ssm`, required: the storage layout of the installation's secrets, `v5`, the only one: the module first, `<root>/internal/<module>/` and `<root>/external/<module>/` (docs/decisions/0072-storage-layout-v5-module-first.md). Layout `v4` was removed in v1.77.1 (an installation still on it migrates with `sluis migrate v5` of v1.77.0 first), and with it the reading of an absent layout as `v4`.

readCache.description: `ssm`: how long a process keeps a document it read; a write drops it. `0s` is off. SLUIS_SECRETS_READ_CACHE_TTL overrides.

refresh.description: `ssm`: how old a secret's copy may be before it is read again: a rotated secret reaches every instance within it.

region.description: `ssm`: the region. Unset follows the AWS SDK's own resolution.

root.description: `file`: the directory the secrets are mounted under. `ssm`: the installation's root, /sluis/<instance>.

source.description: `env`: the variable SLUIS_SECRET_<NAME> (the name upper-cased, every other character an underscore), for a local run. `file`: the file <root>/<name>, read on every use, so a rotated mount takes effect without a restart. `ssm`: a SecureString in AWS SSM Parameter Store under <root> (/sluis/<instance>), on layout v5 (`layout`): a name the service knows is read at its module's address (`<root>/internal/oidc/state-secret`, ...), any other at `<root>/internal/config/<name>`.

secureCookies.description: Mark session cookies Secure. Unset follows the scheme the browser will use: https in the URL. `false` is for a plain-http local run: the service refuses it when `issuerURL` or `publicRootURL` is https.

signingKey.description: The issuer's signing keys: provisioned, never minted here.

activationDelay.description: How long a newly published key waits before a replica signs with it. At least `pollInterval`.

additionalFiles.description: Every OTHER algorithm this installation signs with at once, one file per algorithm.

file.description: The primary key. Unset generates one for this process, which a local run may do and nothing else should. Exclusive with `kms`.

kms.description: Sign with AWS KMS keys instead of a file: the private key never leaves KMS. Exclusive with `file`.

additional.description: Every OTHER algorithm this installation signs with at once, each on its own rotation track, as `signingKey.additionalFiles` does for files. RS256 is the one that exists: for relying parties that need it (Kargo, EKS's OIDC provider).

keys.description: RSA_2048, RSA_3072 or RSA_4096 SIGN_VERIFY keys, oldest first, the last signing; same rotation rules as `keys`.

ECC_NIST_P384 SIGN_VERIFY keys, as ids, ARNs or aliases, oldest first. The LAST signs; the earlier ones stay published until `overlap` after the next one activates. Rotation appends a key. The role needs kms:Sign and kms:GetPublicKey on each.

region.description: The keys' region. Unset follows the AWS SDK's own resolution.

stateSecret.description: The secret (`issuer/state-secret`) holding at least 32 random bytes as base64 or hex (`openssl rand -base64 32`), the same in every replica (a replica whose secret differs refuses to start), from which the sign-in state is derived: a KMS key has no private bytes to derive from.

kmsWrapped.description: Sign with key pairs AWS KMS generates and wraps under ONE symmetric key (the `kms-wrapped` adapter): a new pair per algorithm every `rotateEvery`, published before it signs and kept after it is replaced. The private key is decrypted into process memory to sign. Exclusive with `file` and `kms`.

algorithms.description: The algorithms signed with, the first the installation default. Unset is ES384 and RS256. EdDSA is not supported yet.

keyId.description: DEPRECATED, accepted for one release with a warning: name the symmetric key as `keys.sign` instead. An alias given here is mapped onto `keys.sign`; an ARN or an id is refused.

prepublish.description: How long a new key is published before anything signs with it: longer than any verifier caches the key set (Envoy's jwt_authn: 10m; an hour is common), and shorter than `rotateEvery`. Unset is half of `rotateEvery`, and never shorter than `activationDelay`.

region.description: The key's region. Unset follows the AWS SDK's own resolution.

retain.description: How long a replaced key stays published: at least `lifetimes.token` plus a skew margin. Unset is `overlap`.

rotateEvery.description: How often a new key pair is generated for each algorithm. Longer than `prepublish`, at most 168h.

stateSecret.description: The secret (`issuer/state-secret`) holding at least 32 random bytes as base64 or hex, the same in every replica, from which the sign-in state is derived: a wrapped key is replaced daily and the state must outlive it.

overlap.description: How long a rotated key stays published. Unset is `lifetimes.token` plus a margin for clock skew.

pollInterval.description: How often the files are re-read.

verifyOnly.description: PUBLIC keys published in the JWKS and never signed with, so tokens an earlier signer issued keep verifying until they expire: the overlap of a cutover from file keys to `kmsWrapped`. Each is dropped from the JWKS at its `until`. A private key stops the start.

alg.description: The key's algorithm. Unset follows the key.

preset.description: A key of `cloudflare.presets` that has an `endpoint` (an R2 preset).

credentialsRef.description: Where the credentials for `endpoint` are, in the installation's secrets store (the ssm secrets source): the internal address, `internal/<module>/<name>`, of the `s3-credentials/v1` document (`access_key_id`, `secret_access_key`) that holds static credentials, or `external/cloudflare/<preset>`, the `cloudflare/v1` document the Cloudflare module rotates for an R2 preset with `store: external` (the access key is the token's id; it is read again with a third of its time left and after a 403). Read at start and again after an answer of 403, at most once a minute. Needs `endpoint`; `region` defaults to `auto` with it. Any other address is refused. This is the simple way and needs no `cloudflare` section in this document, so it is the one to use when the presets are another module's (`cloudflare.remote`).

endpoint.description: Overrides the S3 address: LocalStack or an S3-compatible store (Cloudflare R2, MinIO).

dynamodb.description: The DynamoDB tables of the `dynamodb` adapter: one table per module (`tables`, layout v5). Credentials are the platform's (EKS Pod Identity, IRSA, a Lambda role) and are never configured here; an S3-compatible `endpoint` with no such identity names a credentials document by address (`credentialsRef`), never by value.

awsIdentity.description: How the pod gets its AWS role. `pod-identity` (EKS Pod Identity) renders nothing: the association is made outside the chart. `irsa` annotates the account with `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: <awsRoleArn>`, which it requires.

verifyOnly.description: PUBLIC keys the chart mounts from a ConfigMap (they are not secret), one file each at /var/run/access-issuer/verify-keys/<index>.pem, for `config.signingKey.verifyOnly[<index>].file`: published in the JWKS and never signed with. A private key is refused.

pem.description: A PEM public key, a certificate, or a JWK.

slackApps.description: Slack Apps declared as data, created and installed from the console. The service validates the whole catalogue again at start, and refuses an entry for a workspace the policy's slack.workspaces does not name.

push.description: Copy this App's bot token to a secret store with an External Secrets PushSecret: that one key only, to the store and path named here. Absent pushes nothing.

workspace.description: A key of the policy's slack.workspaces.

slackState.description: A recovery copy of the Slack state: see push.

push.description: Copy the credential of every connected Slack workspace, and the mirror of the records that say which workspaces and Slack Connect channels the console holds, to a secret store with an External Secrets PushSecret, for recovery: each whole Secret bundled under its own remote key (remoteKey for the credentials, recordsRemoteKey for the records), because the key names inside are not stable. Absent pushes nothing. deletionPolicy is deliberately not settable -- the case this exists for is the Secret going away.

telemetry.description: The OpenTelemetry SDK environment on every pod of `renders: app` (ADR 0006). Nothing is rendered without `otlp.endpoint`.

endpoint.description: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: an http(s) URL naming the collector or gateway. Empty: nothing is exported and nothing is rendered.

extraEnv.description: Other OpenTelemetry SDK variables, name to value. Every name starts with OTEL_ and none is OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (checked at render).
